claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic fields.
The unchanged alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied pressure fields.
The unchanged alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is prone to cracking.
The alloy's caloric response arises from an inherent phase transformation.
Aging at approximately 650°C for 30 minutes followed by rapid quenching will form nanoscale precipitates.
The precipitates will be uniformly dispersed at grain boundaries and within grains.
The precipitated secondary phases will be ductile.
The aging treatment will produce precipitation hardening.
The fine precipitates will hinder crack initiation.
The fine precipitates will hinder crack propagation.
The precipitates will have a low volume fraction.
The low volume fraction and nanoscale size of the precipitates will minimally perturb the caloric phase transformation.
The aging treatment will increase fracture toughness relative to the untreated alloy.
The aging treatment will reduce cracking relative to the untreated alloy.
The aging treatment will cause little to no degradation of caloric-response magnitude relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed treatment and outcomes apply near room temperature under magnetic- and pressure-field refrigeration operation.
Precipitation hardening is known to improve mechanical integrity in similar high-entropy alloy systems.

contradictions.description: The treatment is called a post-solution aging treatment, but the stated initial material is as-cast and neither the intervention nor the experimental design includes a solution-treatment step before aging.
